question_text: A NOTAM states an airspace restriction in "Class Bravo." Which letter does "Bravo" represent?
explanation_correct: "Bravo" is the ICAO phonetic word for the letter "B". Class B (Bravo) airspace surrounds the busiest airports and requires ATC authorization before entering.

explanation_distractors.B: "Delta" is the phonetic for "D". Class D airspace surrounds smaller airports with control towers.
explanation_distractors.C: "Papa" is the phonetic for "P". Class P is Prohibited airspace.

question_text: What does "Mayday Mayday Mayday" indicate in radio communications?

options.text: A life-threatening emergency requiring immediate assistance
An urgency condition requiring priority handling
A request to change radio frequency

explanation_correct: "Mayday" (from French m'aidez, "help me") repeated three times is the international distress call for a life-threatening emergency. For a less critical urgency, the phrase "Pan-Pan" is used instead.

explanation_distractors.B: "Pan-Pan" (repeated three times) indicates an urgency condition. "Mayday" is reserved for life-threatening emergencies only.
explanation_distractors.C: Changing frequencies uses phrases like "switching to [frequency]" — not a distress call.

question_text: When a controller says "N12345, taxi to runway two-seven," what does "two-seven" mean?

options.text: Runway 27 — the 27th runway on the airport
Taxi to a parking spot numbered 27

explanation_correct: Runway numbers represent the magnetic heading divided by 10. "Two-seven" = Runway 27 = approximately 270° magnetic (due West). Controllers use spoken numbers for each digit to avoid misunderstanding.

explanation_distractors.B: Runway numbers are NOT sequential IDs. They represent the approximate magnetic heading for takeoff/landing. Runway 27 ≈ 270°.
explanation_distractors.C: Runway numbers indicate the direction of flight, not a parking spot number. "Taxi to runway two-seven" means runway 27.

question_text: What is the correct phonetic pronunciation of the letter "C" per ICAO standards?
explanation_correct: "Charlie" (pronounced CHAR LEE or SHAR LEE) is the ICAO phonetic word for "C". It is universally recognized in aviation worldwide.

explanation_distractors.B: "Cuba" is not an ICAO phonetic word. The correct word for "C" is "Charlie".
explanation_distractors.C: "Cobra" is not an ICAO phonetic word. The correct word for "C" is "Charlie".
